chunks: Thus were the wicked people rooted out of existence to the last. All praise be to God, the Lord of all the worlds.

key_terms.الْعَالَمِينَ: The worlds or all existing beings.
key_terms.دَابِرَ: The last generation or descendants; here referring to the final remnant of a people.
key_terms.ظَلَمُوا: They were unjust or wronged themselves.

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the 'last generation' of a people is cut off?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of 'Qut' (extinction), illustrating how divine justice culminates in the total removal of a corrupt generation, serving as a historical precedent for the fate of the disbelievers in the time of the Prophet. The transition to 'Al-hamdu lillah' signifies that the eradication of evil is a manifestation of God's mercy and sovereignty, reinforcing the theological principle that punishment is not merely retributive but also purificatory for the cosmos.
